The ordering of these questions is deliberate and is used to distinguish between individuals who self-diagnose and individuals who have been diagnosed by a health professional. Individuals are first asked if they have a current respiratory allergy, if they respond with "yes", they will be then asked if the allergy was diagnosed by a health professional.
Similar yet distinguished variables include HAYFEVERYR and RALLERGYR. HAYFEVERYR refers to having respiratory allergy symptoms due to only hay fever and RALLERGYR refers to having respiratory allergy symptoms due to allergies excluding hay fever.
For related allergy variables see FALLERGYR.

var.name: RETEV
var.labl: Ever told had intellectual disability
var.txt:
RETEV reports whether the person has an intellectual disability, also known as mental retardation. Please see Comparability and Universe tabs for changes in universe and question wording between samples. This question specifies that the person was told by a doctor or health professional. Health professionals include school psychologists and school nurses.  The Field Representative's Manual states, "Mental Retardation refers to someone who is significantly below average in intellectual functioning, in addition to having problems with adaptive behavior." This official definition was not routinely quoted as part of the interview process and presumably would have been cited only if a subject asked for clarification.
In 1994 and 1995, this variable is part of the Disability Supplement (NHIS-D) that collects information on disability. NHIS-D included two household interviews: in Phase I all members of sample families were screened for any indication of disability; in Phase IIÂ persons with any indication of disability were followed-up for additional information. Phase I includes sensory, communication, and mobility problems; health conditions; activities of daily living and independent activities of daily living; functional limitations; mental health; services and benefits; special health needs of children; early child development; education; relationship to respondent; and perceived disability. Phase II includes four Disability Followback Survey (DFS) questionnaires: one for children, one for adults, one for elderly persons (69 years of age and over) without any indication of disability (also called the Supplement on Aging or SOA; only in 1994), and one for persons with a history of polio.Related Variables Information was collected separately on ADD/ADHD (Attention Deficit Disorder/Attention Deficit Hyperactive Disorder) (ADDEV) for sample children aged 2 to 17 and on "Other Developmental Delay" (ODDEV) for all sample children. Prior to 2022, information was collected on one of the main causes of mental retardation, Down Syndrome (DOWNSYNEV). To see if the sample person currently has an intellectual disability, see INTDSNW.
Intellectual disability, also known as mental retardation was also incorporated into the survey as one of the possible conditions or health problems that respondents could select from a list on a flash card, to explain why individuals were limited in their activities. Starting 2019, flash cards were eliminated.

var.name: INTDSNW
var.labl: Currently has intellectual disability
var.txt: For sample children with an intellectual disability diagnosis (RETEV), INTDSNW indicates if the child currently has an intellectual disability, also known as mental retardation.

var.name: SALLERGYR
var.labl: Had skin allergy, past 12 months
var.txt:
SALLERGYR identifies sample children (and sample adults in 2010, 2012 and 2021) who had eczema or any kind of skin allergy during the past 12 months.
Interviewers asked the broad opening question, "During the past 12 months, has [name] had any of the following conditions?" with eczema or skin allergy among the many conditions named. The inquiry did not specify that the eczema or skin allergy had to be diagnosed by a doctor or other health professional, nor did it limit allowed responses to allergies of a particular severity (i.e., those severe enough to require treatment or medication).
The Field Representative's Manual for 2001 forward defined eczema as "an acute, or chronic, noncontagious, itching inflammatory disease of the skin." This definition was not routinely shared with respondents.
Related Skin Problem Variables In 2007, respondents were asked if during the past 12 months sample children had severe acne (ACNEYR), warts (WARTSYR), or a skin problem other than eczema, acne, or warts (SKINOTHYR).
For sample adults in 2002 and 2007, a question was included that asked whether sample adults had skin problems during the past 12 months (SKINPROBYR).For more information on related allergy variables see (FALLERGYR).
In 2021, the follow-up question to this variable is represented by SKINALLERGY. The ordering of these questions is deliberate and is used to distinguish between individuals who self-diagnose and individuals who have been diagnosed by a health professional. Individuals are first asked if they have a current skin allergy, if they respond with "yes", they will be then asked if the allergy was diagnosed by a health professional.
In 2010, the survey asked a number of follow-up questions about dermatitis and jobs held. For more information, see DRMDEV.

var.name: SKINALLERGY
var.labl: Ever been diagnosed with skin allergy
var.txt:
For sample adults and sample children with a current skin allergy (SALLERGYR), SKINALLERGY indicates whether they have been diagnosed by a doctor or health professional with eczema or atopic dermatitis. This is a follow-up question to SALLERGYR. The ordering of these questions is deliberate and is used to distinguish between individuals who self-diagnose and individuals who have been diagnosed by a health professional. Individuals are first asked if they have a current skin allergy, if they respond with "yes", they will be then asked if the allergy was diagnosed by a health professional.
For related allergy variables see FALLERGYR.

var.name: SMELLDIFF
var.labl: Difficulty smelling
var.txt:
For sample adults, SMELLDIFF reports the level of difficulty the respondent had with their sense of smell or ability to detect odors in the past 12 months. Respondents were asked whether they had no difficulty, a little difficulty, moderate difficulty, a lot of difficulty, or no sense of smell at all. This question associated with this variable was asked to sample adults only in 2021, and to sample adults and sample children in 2024.
SMELLDIFF is one of several questions sponsored by the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) to gather information on smell and taste disorders in adults. For more information and a complete list of these variables, see the description for TSTSMDOC.

var.name: SMELLODOR
var.labl: Smell unpleasant odor
var.txt:
For sample adults, SMELLODOR reports whether the respondent sometimes smelled an unpleasant, bad, metallic, or burning odor when nothing was there, in the past 12 months. This question associated with this variable was asked to sample adults only in 2021, and to sample adults and sample children in 2024.
SMELLODOR is one of several questions sponsored by the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) to gather information on smell and taste disorders in adults. For more information and a complete list of these variables, see the description for TSTSMDOC.

var.name: SMELLPAST
var.labl: Smelling compared to past
var.txt:
For sample adults, SMELLPAST reports if and how the respondentâs ability to smell has changed compared to when they were 25 years old, or 5 years younger if they were 25 years old or younger at the time of the survey. Respondents were asked if their smell was better, worse, or if there was no change.
SMELLPAST is one of several questions sponsored by the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) to gather information on smell and taste disorders in adults. For more information and a complete list of these variables, see the description for TSTSMDOC.

var.name: STROKEV
var.labl: Ever told had a stroke
var.txt:
STROKEV identifies adults whom a doctor or other health professional ever diagnosed as having had a stroke. In 2002 and 2007, persons who had ever been diagnosed with a stroke were asked whether they had a stroke during the past 12 months (STROKEYR). Please see Comparability and Universe tabs for complete information on universe changes between samples.
The Field Representative's Manual for 1997-2000 directed interviewers to "include strokes, cerebrovascular accidents, and brain hemorrhages," but this directive was not stated during the interview. Stroke was defined in the Field Representative's Manual for 2001 forward as "a cerebral hemorrhage or embolism of the cerebral blood vessels," but this definition was not routinely shared with respondents.
Related Variables Information on whether persons age 20 and older ever had a stroke is also available in 1977 (STROKEWOC). The information included in STROKEWOC was collected via two separate lines of questioning. Interviewers asked, "Has [name] ever had a stroke?" and "Has a doctor ever told [name] he had a stroke?" In addition, the person was recorded as having had a stroke and asked about a doctor's diagnosis of the condition if "stroke" was reported as the reason why an individual was limited in daily activities (i.e., "needs the help of another person in getting around," "stays in bed all or most of the day," "needs help in bathing/dressing/eating/using the toilet").
Only cases coded as "2" (Yes, medically confirmed) in STROKEWOC are roughly comparable to cases with an affirmative response in STROKEV. Along with the notable difference in question wording for the two variables, there is a difference in the range of responses that were accepted. In the 1977 inquiry, interviewers were directed to reask the question if a term other than "stroke" (such as "brain hemorrhage") was reported, and to consider as a "No" response any term other than "stroke." By contrast, as noted above, for STROKEV, other terms such as "cerebral hemorrhage" and "cerebrovascular accident" were accepted as "Yes" responses.

var.name: TASTEDIFF
var.labl: In the last 12 months, how difficult to taste
var.txt:
For sample adults, TASTEDIFF asks them to report how difficult it is to taste sweet, sour, salty, or bitter foods and drinks.
TASTEDIFF is one of several questions sponsored by the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) to gather information on smell and taste disorders in adults. For more information and a complete list of these variables, see the description for TSTSMDOC.

var.name: TASTEUNWANT
var.labl: In the last 12 months, ever had unwanted taste or sensation in mouth
var.txt:
For sample adults, TASTEUNWANT indicates whether they had an unwanted taste or sensation in their mouth that would not go away, in the last 12 months.
TASTEUNWANT is one of several questions sponsored by the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) to gather information on smell and taste disorders in adults. For more information and a complete list of these variables, see the description for TSTSMDOC.

var.name: TASTECHG
var.labl: Ability to taste compared to 5 years prior or at the age of 25
var.txt:
For sample adults, TASTECHG asks them to rate their ability to taste sweet, sour, salty, or bitter foods and drinks compared to 5 years ago or at the age of 25.
The 2021 field manual states the following: All adults will also be asked to compare their ability to smell, to taste sweet, sour, salty, or bitter foods and drinks, and to taste flavors such as chocolate, vanilla, or strawberry compared to when they were 25 or were 5 years younger than their current age if they are less than 30. Those who have problems will be asked whether they have discussed any problem with a doctor or other health professional, and if so, when was the last time.TASTECHG is one of several questions sponsored by the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) to gather information on smell and taste disorders in adults. For more information and a complete list of these variables, see the description for TSTSMDOC.

var.name: TASTEID
var.labl: Ability to taste specific flavors compared to 5 years prior or at the age of 25
var.txt:
For sample adults, TASTEID asks them to rate their ability to specific flavors such as chocolate, vanilla, or strawberry compared to 5 years ago or at the age of 25.
The 2021 field manual states the following: All adults will also be asked to compare their ability to smell, to taste sweet, sour, salty, or bitter foods and drinks, and to taste flavors such as chocolate, vanilla, or strawberry compared to when they were 25 or were 5 years younger than their current age if they are less than 30. Those who have problems will be asked whether they have discussed any problem with a doctor or other health professional, and if so, when was the last time.TASTEID is one of several questions sponsored by the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) to gather information on smell and taste disorders in adults. For more information and a complete list of these variables, see the description for TSTSMDOC.

var.name: TSTSMDOCWHN
var.labl: Last time talked to doctor about difficulty in taste and smell
var.txt:
For respondents who discussed problems with or changes in ability to taste or smell with a doctor or health professional (TSTSMDOC), TSTSMDOCWHN indicates how long since the last time they spoke to a doctor or health professional about their problems with their ability to taste and smell. This question associated with this variable was asked to sample adults only in 2021, and to sample adults and sample children in 2024.
TSTSMDOCWHN is one of several questions sponsored by the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) to gather information on smell and taste disorders in adults. For more information and a complete list of these variables, see the description for TSTSMDOC.

var.name: COPDEV
var.labl: Ever been told you had COPD
var.txt:
For sample adults, COPDEV reports if the person has ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that they have Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), emphysema, or chronic bronchitis. Prior to 2019, the question only explicitly asked about COPD, but the Field Representative's Manuals defined Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) as "a group of diseases that cause airflow blockage and breathing-related problems. It includes emphysema, chronic bronchitis, and in some cases asthma".
Beginning with 2012, this question on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) was sponsored by the National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (NCCDPHP, CDC). Prior to 2019, it was a core question in Adult Conditions module and, beginning in 2019, it is part of the annual core for the Sample Adult interview. Before 2012, the NHIS collected data on chronic bronchitis and emphysema (items from which a measure of COPD can be developed), but did not address COPD directly.
A report on the cognitive evaluation of this item is available on the CDC's Q-Bank question evaluation website.

var.name: PSOREV
var.labl: Ever told had psoriasis
var.txt:
PSOREV identifies sample adults who were ever told by a doctor or other health professional that they had psoriasis.
The 2023 Field Representative's Manuals provides the information that psoriasis "is a chronic autoimmune skin disease that speeds up the growth cycle of skin cells."
The question associated with the variable was included in the Sponsored Conditions-Ever (SCE) supplement and sponsored by the National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC/NCCDPHP).

var.name: ASTHATAKYR
var.labl: Had asthma attack/episode, past 12 months
var.txt:
For sample adults and sample children who were ever told by a doctor or other health professional that they had asthma (ASTHMAEV), ASTHATAKYR identifies those who had an asthma attack/episode during the past 12 months.
Those who responded affirmatively to ASTHATAKYR were asked a follow-up question about whether they "had to visit an emergency room or urgent care center because of asthma" during the past 12 months (ASTHERYR).
Other asthma-related questions were periodically included in the survey; see ASTHMAEV for a summary of these variables currently in the IPUMS NHIS.

var.name: ASTHERYR
var.labl: Visited ER for asthma, past 12 months
var.txt: For sample adults and sample children who were ever told by a doctor or other health professional that they had asthma (ASTHMAEV), and, from 1997-2009, who had an asthma episode/attack in the past 12 months (ASTHATAKYR), ASTHERYR identifies those who visited an emergency room or urgent care center because of their asthma during the past 12 months.

var.name: CNBLAD
var.labl: Ever had cancer: Bladder
var.txt:
CNBLAD identifies sample adults who had ever been told that they had bladder cancer. Those sample adults who reported ever being told by a doctor or other health professional that they had cancer or a malignancy of any kind (CANCEREV) were asked the follow-up question, "What kind of cancer was it?"
Interviewers marked up to three kinds of cancer specified on the survey form, and noted when the respondent mentioned more than three types of cancer. For 1997 forward, the Field Representative's Manual directed: "Count the same type of cancer or malignancy on different body parts as only one kind. For example, malignant moles on the face, neck, and trunk should be counted as only one kind of cancer." Interviewers were further directed to not read the answer categories on the survey form to respondents. If the respondent used a technical term not on the form, then the interviewer was to "ask what part of the body this affected and enter that"; if the answer did not fit a category on the form, then the interviewer was to mark "other" and write down the response.
The coded responses to "What kind of cancer was it?" were the basis of a series of dichotomous variables, each indicating whether a particular type of cancer, such as bladder cancer, was mentioned by a respondent who was ever diagnosed with cancer.
Related Variables Other dichotomous variables in this series identify sample adults mentioning the following types of cancer:
blood cancer (CNBLOD)
bone cancer (CNBONE)
brain cancer (CNBRAN)
breast cancer (CNBRES)
cervical cancer (CNCERV)
colon cancer (CNCOLN)
esophageal cancer (CNESOP)
gallbladder cancer (CNGALL)
kidney cancer (CNKIDN)
larynx-windpipe cancer (CNLARX)
leukemia (CNLEUK)
liver cancer (CNLIVR)
lung cancer (CNLUNG)
lymphoma (CNLYMP)
melanoma (CNMELN)
mouth, lip, or tongue cancer (CNMOTH)
ovarian cancer (CNOVAR)
pancreatic cancer (CNPANC)
prostate cancer (CNPROS)
rectal cancer (CNRECT)
(melanoma) skin cancer (CNSKMELN)
(non-melanoma) skin cancer (CNSKNM)
skin cancer of an unknown type (CNSKDK)
soft tissue (muscle or fat) cancer (CNSOFT)
stomach cancer (CNSTOM)
testicular cancer (CNTEST)
throat-pharynx cancer (CNTHRO)
thyroid cancer (CNTHYR)
uterine cancer (CNUTER) Those who mentioned any other kind of cancer not previously listed are identified in CNOTHR, while those who mentioned having been diagnosed with more than three types of cancer are identified in CNKIND3.
Interviewers asked the additional follow-up question, "How old were you when [this cancer] was first diagnosed?" This information was again collected for up to three specific types of cancer. Age at first diagnosis of bladder cancer is reported in CNBLADAG.

var.txt:
For sample adults who had ever been told that they had bladder cancer (CNBLAD), CNBLADAG reports how old the person was when bladder cancer was first diagnosed.

var.name: CNOTHR
var.labl: Ever had cancer: Other kind
var.txt:
CNOTHR identifies sample adults age 18 and older who had ever been told that they had some kind of cancer other than those kinds specified in other public use cancer type recodes. Before 2018, CNOTHR identifies whether sample adults and older had some kind of cancer other than the list of 29 different cancer types listed below under the "Related Variables" heading (with the exception of skin melanoma cancer (CNSKMELN). Those sample adults who reported ever being told by a doctor or other health professional that they had cancer or a malignancy of any kind (CANCEREV) were asked the follow-up question, "What kind of cancer was it?"
Interviewers marked up to three kinds of cancer specified on the survey form, and noted when the respondent mentioned more than three types of cancer. The 1997-2000 Field Representative's Manual directed, "Count the same type of cancer or malignancy on different body parts as only one kind. For example, malignant moles on the face, neck, and trunk should be counted as only one kind of cancer." Interviewers were further directed to not read the answer categories on the survey form to respondents. If the respondent used a technical term not on the form, then the interviewer was to "ask what part of the body this affected and enter that"; if the answer did not fit a category on the form, then the interviewer was to mark "other" and write down the response.
The coded responses to "What kind of cancer was it?" were the basis of a series of dichotomous variables, each indicating whether a particular type of cancer was mentioned by a respondent who was ever diagnosed with cancer.
Related Variables The term "other kind of cancer" refers to a type of cancer other than the following specific types of cancer, each of which was the subject of a separate dichotomous variable:
bladder cancer (CNBLAD)
blood cancer (CNBLOD)
bone cancer (CNBONE)
brain cancer (CNBRAN)
breast cancer (CNBRES)
cervical cancer (CNCERV)
colon cancer (CNCOLN)
esophageal cancer (CNESOP)
gallbladder cancer (CNGALL)
kidney cancer (CNKIDN)
larynx-windpipe cancer (CNLARX)
leukemia (CNLEUK)
liver cancer (CNLIVR)
lung cancer (CNLUNG)
lymphoma (CNLYMP)
melanoma (CNMELN)
mouth, lip, or tongue cancer (CNMOTH)
ovarian cancer (CNOVAR)
pancreatic cancer (CNPANC)
prostate cancer (CNPROS)
(melanoma) skin cancer (CNSKMELN)
rectal cancer (CNRECT)
(non-melanoma) skin cancer (CNSKNM)
skin cancer of an unknown type (CNSKDK)
soft tissue (muscle or fat) cancer (CNSOFT)
stomach cancer (CNSTOM)
testicular cancer (CNTEST)
throat-pharynx cancer (CNTHRO)
thyroid cancer (CNTHYR)
uterine cancer (CNUTER)
Those who mentioned having been diagnosed with more than three types of cancer are identified in CNKIND3.
Interviewers asked the additional follow-up question, "How old were you when [this cancer] was first diagnosed?" This information was again collected for up to three specific types of cancer. Age at first diagnosis of some kind of cancer other than those specified above is reported in CNOTHRAG.

var.name: CANCERNO
var.labl: Number of kinds of cancer
var.txt: For sample adults, CANCERNO reports a count of the total number of different kinds of cancer they report ever having been told they had by a doctor or other health professional. Prior to 2019, CANCERNO was only asked of sample adults who were ever diagnosed with cancer. Beginning in 2019, this variable is topcoded at 4+ cancers, whereas it was topcoded at 6+ cancers in 1992.

var.name: DIABETICAGE
var.labl: Age first diagnosed with diabetes
var.txt:
DIABETICAGE reports age at first diagnosis by a doctor of "diabetes or sugar diabetes," for sample adults who were ever told by a doctor or other health professional that they had diabetes (other than during pregnancy alone or prediabetes) (DIABETICEV). Persons who reported their diagnosis as "borderline" diabetes were not asked this follow-up question. The Field Representative's Manual for 1997-2000 directed interviewers to probe for a specific age but to "record a best estimate if that is what the sample adult gives you."
The 2006 Codebook for the NHIS public use data files contains the following warning about inaccuracies in this variable: These data have not been edited for reasonableness. Some respondents appear to give information on how long ago the condition was first diagnosed rather than their age when the condition was first diagnosed.Other diabetes-related questions were periodically included in the survey; see DIABETICEV for a summary of these variables currently in the IPUMS NHIS.

catgry.labl: Have pre, potential, or borderline diabetes

var.name: DIABTYPE
var.labl: Type of diabetes
var.txt: For sample adults who have ever been told they have diabetes by a doctor or other health professional (DIABETICEV), DIABTYPE reports the type of diabetes they have.

var.name: INSULIN
var.labl: Now taking insulin
var.txt:
INSULIN reports responses to the question, "Are you now taking insulin?" The U.S. Food and Drug Administration website on diabetes information notes that insulin is taken by diabetics to control blood sugar levels and that insulin cannot be taken by mouth because it would be destroyed by digestion. Instead, insulin is injected through shots or other devices such as insulin pens, jet injectors, or pumps.
Respondents who received the question associated with INSULIN were also asked if they were currently taking diabetic pills, also called oral agents or oral hypoglycemic agents, to lower their blood sugar (DIAPILLS).
Related Variables Starting in 2021, the following diabetes related variables were introduced:
Delayed buying insulin, past 12m (DELAYINSL)
Took less insulin, past 12m (LESSINSL)
Skipped insulin, past 12m (SKIPINSL)

var.name: DIAPILLS
var.labl: Now taking diabetic pills
var.txt:
For sample adults age 18 and older who have ever been told they have diabetes or prediabetes, DIAPILLS reports responses to the question, "Are you now taking diabetic pills to lower your blood sugar? These are sometimes called oral agents or oral hypoglycemic agents."
Respondents who received the question associated with DIAPILLS were also asked if they were currently taking insulin (INSULIN). Insulin cannot be taken orally; instead, it must be injected through shots or other devices such as insulin pens, jet injectors, or pumps.

var.name: DIAGLP
var.labl: Taking GLP-1 injectable medication(s)
var.txt:
For sample adults who were told they had prediabetes and/or diabetes (DIAPRE, DIABETICEV), DIAGLP indicates whether the respondent reported taking any injectable medications other than insulin to lower their blood sugar or lose weight. If necessary during the interview, enumerators would list respondents several brands of GLP-1 injectables as examples of such injectable medications.
This variable was added as annual core content in the 2024 NHIS Diabetes (DIB) section.

var.name: DIAYRSAGO
var.labl: Years since first diagnosed with diabetes
var.txt:
For sample adults who were ever told by a doctor or other health professional that they had diabetes (excluding pregnancy and prediabetes) (DIABETICEV), DIAYRSAGO reports the number of years since they were first diagnosed with diabetes.
DIAYRSAGO is a recoded variable calculated as the difference between current age (AGE) and reported age at the onset of diabetes (DIABETICAGE). The Codebooks for 1999 forward note, "For persons age 85 or older, this difference may be an underestimate" due to the fact that both AGE and DIABETICAGE are topcoded at age 85. Persons who had been diagnosed with "borderline diabetes" (in DIABETICEV) were not asked the follow-up question about age at onset of diabetes.

catgry.labl: 1+ years w diabetes and age is 85+
Diagnosed at age 85+ and is age 85+

var.name: DIAPRE
var.labl: Ever been told you have prediabetes
var.txt:
For sample adults and sample children, DIAPRE reports if the respondent was ever told by a doctor or health professional that they have prediabetes. In 2006, this variable was only available for sample adults who had never been told they had diabetes or were told they had borderline diabetes.
For related variables, please see DIABETICEV or use the IPUMS NHIS search function and drop-down menus.

var.name: DIADIAGPREG
var.labl: First told had diabetes, sugar diabetes, or gestational diabetes during pregnancy
var.txt:
For female sample adults aged 18 and older (and in 2016 and 2017, who have ever been pregnant), this variable reports if the person was ever told by a doctor of other health professional that they had diabetes, sugar diabetes, or gestational diabetes during their pregnancy.
In 2016 and 2017, this variable was part of the Sample Adult Diabetes supplement, sponsored by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) and National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (NCCDPHP).

var.name: DIAINSLLONG
var.labl: Length of time before started insulin after diagnosed w/ diabetes
var.txt:
For sample adults with diabetes who now take insulin by shot or pump (INSULIN), DIAINSLLONG reports the length of time between when they were first diagnosed with diabetes and when they started taking insulin.
This variable is part of the Sample Adult Diabetes supplement, sponsored by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) and National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (NCCDPHP).

var.name: DIAINSLSTOP
var.labl: Stopped taking insulin for more than 6 months
var.txt:
For sample adults with diabetes who now take insulin by shot or pump (INSULIN), DIAINSLSTOP reports if the person has ever stopped taking insulin for more than six months after they started taking insulin.
This variable is part of the Sample Adult Diabetes supplement, sponsored by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) and National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (NCCDPHP).

var.name: DIAINSLSTOP1STYR
var.labl: Stopped taking insulin for more than 6 months during the first year after diabetes diagnosis
var.txt:
For sample adults who started taking insulin within a year of being diagnosed with diabetes (DIAINSLLONG) and stopped taking it for more than six months (DIAINSLSTOP), DIAINSLSTOP1STYR reports if the person stopped taking insulin for more than six months only during the first year after their diabetes diagnosis.
This variable is part of the Sample Adult Diabetes supplement, sponsored by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) and National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (NCCDPHP).

var.name: CHOLMEDNOW
var.labl: Now taking prescribed medicine to lower cholesterol
var.txt:
For sample adults who were ever told they have high cholesterol (CHOLHIGHEV), CHOLMEDNOW indicates if they currently take prescribed medication to lower their cholesterol level.
In 1991, 1993, 1998, and 2015-2018, CHOLMEDNOW indicates if sample adults who were ever prescribed medicine for high cholesterol (CHOLMEDPRE) are currently taking medication to lower their cholesterol level. In 2005, CHOLMEDNOW indicates if sample adults, regardless of whether they had been told they have high cholesterol, currently takes prescribed medication regularly, that is, at least 3 times a week, to lower their cholesterol level.

var.name: HYP2TIME
var.labl: Ever told had hypertension on 2+ visits
var.txt: For sample persons or adults aged 18 and over who were ever told they had hypertension or high blood pressure, HYP2TIME reports if they were told they had high blood pressure or hypertension on two or more DIFFERENT visits.

var.name: HYPMEDNOW
var.labl: Now taking prescribed medicine to lower blood pressure
var.txt: For adults who were diagnosed or treated for high blood pressure (or, in 1989, for adults with confirmed diabetes), HYPMEDNOW reports if the person is currently taking medicine prescribed by a doctor to lower blood pressure. Please see Comparability and Universe tabs for information on changes in universe between samples.

var.name: INJANY
var.labl: Any injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults and sample children, INJANY reports whether, in the past 3 months, they had an accident or injury where any part of their body was hurt. Sample adults are given the additional instruction that this excludes any of the injuries they mentioned in response to questions covering repetitive strain injuries (INJREPANY).
INJANY is collected as part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury, fielded for two consecutive years every three years. The 2020 NHIS Survey Description defines sudden injury as injury that: may occur accidently or on purpose, and it may be self-inflicted or caused by others.The sudden injury rotating core includes questions on sudden injury and whether the sudden injury limited usual activities for at least 24 hours following the injury. Such injuries are considered significant injuries. Follow-up questions about the number of significant injuries, the location where they occurred, the activity in which the person was engaged when they occurred, the type of injury (e.g., fall, motor vehicle accident), and medical care following injury were also asked.
In addition to INJANY, variables in the rotating NHIS injury core include:
General Sudden Injury Information  INJSIGNFCNT: Limited by injury for at least 24 hours (significant injury), past 3 months
INJSIGNUM: Number of significant injuries, past 3 months (for sample adults)
INJSIGNUMCH: Number of significant injuries, past 3 months (for sample children) Location and Activity When Significantly Injured  INJSIGHOME: Significant injury occurred at home, past 3 months
INJSIGCHORE: Significant injury occurred while doing chores, past 3 months
INJSIGWORK: Significant injury occurred at work, past 3 months
INJSIGSCH: Significant injury occurred at school/daycare, past 3 months
INJSIGSPOR: Significant injury occurred while playing sports/exercising, past 3 months
INJSIGMOTOR: Significant injury caused by motor vehicle accident or collision, past 3 months
INJSIGMVDRVR: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Was driver
INJSIGMVPSGR: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Was passenger
INJSIGMVBICL: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Was bicyclist
INJSIGMVPDTN: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Was pedestrian
INJSIGMVOTR: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Other Significant Falls  INJSIGFALL: Significant injury occurred due to fall, past 3 months
INJSIGFALHOM: Significant fall occurred at home, past 3 months
INJSIGFALWRK: Significant fall occurred at work, past 3 months
INJSIGFALSCH: Significant fall occurred at school/daycare, past 3 months Care-Seeking for Significant Injury  INJSIGSAWDR: Saw doctor about significant injury, past 3 months
INJSIGER: Went to ER for significant injury, past 3 months
INJSIGHOSP: Hospitalized for significant injury, past 3 months
INJSIGBONES: Any broken bones due to significant injury, past 3 months
INJSIGSTCH: Any stitches or staples due to significant injury, past 3 months Impacts of Significant Injury on Work and School  INJSIGMISWRK: Number of workdays missed due to significant injury, past 3 months
INJSIGFUTWRK: Will miss more workdays due to significant injury in past 3 months
INJSIGSTPWRK: Stopped work or changed jobs due to significant injury, past 3 months
INJSIGCHGWRK: Major change in work activities due to significant injury, past 3 months
INJSIGMISSCH: Number of school days missed due to significant injury, past 3 months
INJSIGFUTSCH: Will miss more school days due to significant injury, past 3 months Traumatic Brain Injury  TBILOSTCONEV: Ever lost consciousness due to blow/jolt to the head
TBIDAZEV: Ever dazed or have gap in memory due to blow/jolt to the head
TBICONSYMPEV: Ever had headache, vomiting, blurred vision, or mood changes after blow/jolt to the head
TBICONCHKEV: Ever checked for concussion or brain injury
TBICONCUSEV: Ever told had concussion or brain injury
TBICONDAZYR: Lost consciousness, dazed or confused, or had gap in memory, past 12 months
TBICONHEADYR: Headache, sensitivities, balance problems or mood change, past 12 months
TBISPORTYR: Blow or jolt to head while playing sports or rec activity, past 12 months
TBILEAGUEYR: Blow or jolt to head while playing organized sports, past 12 months
TBIEVALYR: Evaluated for concussion, past 12 months Repetitive Strain Injury  INJREPANY: Any injury due to repetitive strain, past 3 months
INJREPSIG: Limited by repetitive strain injury for at least 24 hours (significant injury), past 3 months
INJREPSGDR: Saw doctor about significant repetitive strain injury, past 3 months
INJREPSGMSWK: Number of work days missed due to significant repetitive strain injury, past 3 months
INJREPSGFTWK: Will miss more work days due to significant repetitive strain injury, past 3 months
INJREPSGSTWK: Stopped work or changed jobs due to significant repetitive strain injury, past 3 months
INJREPSGCHWK: Major change in work activities due to significant repetitive strain injury, past 3 months
INJREPSGWKRE: Ever told significant repetitive strain injury in past 3 months likely to be work-related Other NHIS Data on Injury The NHIS has adopted several different approaches to the collection of data on injury over time. Most recently, the NHIS questionnaire included an injury and poisoning supplement, fielded annually from 1997 until 2017. For more information on person- and injury-level data from the injury and poisoning supplements, please see our user note. The NHIS Disability Supplement (NHIS-D), fielded in 1994-95, also collected a handful of measures of injury, such as DPADLINJPLACE (Place where injury or accident causing main limiting ADL condition occurred) and DPADLINJURYE (External cause of injury for main limiting ADL condition caused by accident or injury). In addition to the two supplements already mentioned, the NHIS has also fielded other supplements over the years that partially or fully cover injury topics. For example, there are a set of variables on adult conditions that were collected only for 2008 including injury variables such as HEADINJEV (Ever had injury to head or brain).

var.name: INJSIGNFCNT
var.labl: Limited by injury for at least 24 hours (significant injury), past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children who had any injury in the past 3 months (INJANY), INJSIGNFCNT reports whether the injury limited their usual activities for at least 24 hours after the injury occurred.
INJSIGNFCNT is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGHOME
var.labl: Significant injury occurred at home, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children who had a significant injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGHOME reports whether the injury happened at home. If necessary, interviewers elaborated by asking whether the injury happened at home, including the yards, garage, basement, and other places on the home property.
INJSIGHOME is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGSPOR
var.labl: Significant injury occurred while playing sports/exercising, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children ages 3 to 17 who had a significant injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGSPOR reports whether the injury occurred while they were playing sports or exercising, including walking, biking, running, playing a sport such as baseball, basketball, or football, or doing any other physical activity.
INJSIGSPOR is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGFALL
var.labl: Significant injury occurred due to fall, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children who had a significant injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGFALL reports whether the injury occurred due to a fall.
INJSIGFALL is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGFALHOM
var.labl: Significant fall occurred at home, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had two or more significant non-repetitive strain injuries or don't know or refused to report how many injuries they had in the past 3 months and sample children who had two or more significant injuries or don't know or refused to report how many injuries they had in the past 3 months (INJSIGNUM) and who had a significant injury due to a fall (INJSIGFALL), INJSIGFALHOM reports whether they fell at home.
INJSIGFALHOM is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGMOTOR
var.labl: Significant injury caused by a motor vehicle crash or collision, past 3 months
var.txt: For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children who had a significant injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGMOTOR reports whether they were injured as a result of being in a motor vehicle crash or being hit by a motor vehicle while walking or biking. If necessary, interviewers elaborated by stating Motor vehicles include cars, trucks, vans, buses, motorcycles, motorized scooters, motorized wheelchairs, motorized carts, tractors, ATVs, snowmobiles, dune buggies, and other motorized vehicles.INJSIGMOTOR is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGMVDRVR
var.labl: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Was driver
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children ages 6 to 17 who were significantly injured in a motor vehicle accident in the past 3 months (INJSIGMOTOR), INJSIGMVDRVR indicates whether they were the driver in the motor vehicle accident.
INJSIGMVDRVR is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGMVPSGR
var.labl: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Was passenger
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children ages 6 to 17 who were significantly injured in a motor vehicle accident in the past 3 months (INJSIGMOTOR), INJSIGMVPSGR indicates whether they were a passenger in the motor vehicle accident.
INJSIGMVPSGR is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGMVBICL
var.labl: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Was bicyclist
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children ages 6 to 17 who were significantly injured in a motor vehicle accident in the past 3 months (INJSIGMOTOR), INJSIGMVBICL indicates whether they were a bicyclist in the motor vehicle accident.
INJSIGMVBICL is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGMVPDTN
var.labl: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Was pedestrian
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children ages 6 to 17 who were significantly injured in a motor vehicle accident in the past 3 months (INJSIGMOTOR), INJSIGMVPDTN indicates whether they were a pedestrian in the motor vehicle accident.
INJSIGMVPDTN is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGMVOTR
var.labl: Significantly injured in motor vehicle accident, past 3 months: Was other
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children ages 6 to 17 who were significantly injured in a motor vehicle accident in the past 3 months (INJSIGMOTOR), INJSIGMVOTR indicates whether they were doing something other than driving, involved as the passenger, a bicyclist, or a pedestrian during the motor vehicle accident in which they were injured.
INJSIGMVOTR is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGSAWDR
var.labl: Saw doctor about significant injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children who were significantly injured in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGSAWDR reports whether they saw a doctor for their significant injury or injuries.
INJSIGSAWDR is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGER
var.labl: Went to ER for significant injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children who were significantly injured in the past 3 months and saw a doctor for their significant injury or injuries (INJSIGSAWDR) and went to the emergency room at least once in the past year or don't know or refused to say if they went to the emergency room in the past year (ERYRNO), INJSIGER reports whether they went to an emergency room for their significant injury or injuries.
INJSIGER is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGHOSP
var.labl: Hospitalized for significant injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children who were significantly injured in the past 3 months and saw a doctor for their significant injury or injuries (INJSIGSAWDR) and was hospitalized at least once in the past year or don't know or refused to say if they were hospitalized in the past year (HOSPNGHT), INJSIGHOSP reports whether they were hospitalized for their significant injury or injuries.
INJSIGHOSP is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGBONES
var.labl: Any broken bones due to significant injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children who were significantly injured in the past 3 months and saw a doctor for their significant injury or injuries (INJSIGSAWDR), INJSIGBONES reports whether the injury caused any broken bones.
INJSIGBONES is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGSTCH
var.labl: Any stitches or staples due to significant injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months and sample children who were significantly injured in the past 3 months and saw a doctor for their significant injury or injuries (INJSIGSAWDR), INJSIGSTCH reports whether they required any stitches or staples because of their significant injury or injuries.
INJSIGSTCH is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGNUM
var.labl: Number of significant injuries, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGNUM reports the number of significant non-repetitive strain injuries in the past 3 months. A related variable, INJSIGNUMCH, reports the number of significant injuries in the past 3 months for sample children with a significant injury in the past 3 months.
INJSIGNUM is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.
var.codInstr: This is a 2-digit numeric variable with 0 implied decimal places

var.name: INJSIGNUMCH
var.labl: Number of significant injuries for children, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample children who had any injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGNUMCH reports the number of significant injuries in the past 3 months. A related variable, INJSIGNUM, reports the number of significant, non-repetitive injuries in the past 3 months for sample adults who had any injury in the past 3 months.
INJSIGNUMCH is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.
var.codInstr: This is a 2-digit numeric variable with 0 implied decimal places

var.name: INJSIGWORK
var.labl: Significant injury occurred at work, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had two or more significant non-repetitive strain injuries or don't know or refused to report how many injuries they had in the past 3 months (INJSIGNUM) or who had one or more significant non-repetitive strain injuries in the past 3 months but did not report an injury occurring at home (INJSIGHOME), INJSIGWORK reports whether the injury happened at working at a job or business.
INJSIGWORK is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGFALWRK
var.labl: Significant fall occurred at work, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had two or more significant non-repetitive strain injuries or don't know or refused to report how many injuries they had in the past 3 months (INJSIGNUM) and had a significant injury due to a fall (INJSIGFALL) and were also injured at work (INJSIGWORK), INJSIGFALWRK reports whether they fell at work.
INJSIGFALHOM is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGCHORE
var.labl: Significant injury occurred while doing chores, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGCHORE reports whether the injury happened while they were doing household activities such as housework, cooking, home maintenance, or yard work.
INJSIGCHORE is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGMISWRK
var.labl: Number of work days missed due to significant injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who had a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGMISWRK reports the number of workdays they missed due to the injury.
INJSIGMISWRK is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.
var.codInstr: This is a 2-digit numeric variable with 0 implied decimal places

var.name: INJSIGFUTWRK
var.labl: Will miss more work days due to significant injury in past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who missed at least one day of work due to a significant non-repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGMISWRK), INJSIGFUTWRK reports whether they expect to miss any more days of work due to the injury.
INJSIGFUTWRK is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGSTPWRK
var.labl: Stopped work or changed jobs due to significant injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who missed zero or more days of work due to significant sudden injury in the past 3 months or refused to say or don't know how many days they missed due to injury (INJSIGMISWRK), INJSIGSTPWRK reports whether they changed jobs or stopped work due to significant injury.
INJSIGSTPWRK is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGCHGWRK
var.labl: Major change in work activities due to significant injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults who missed zero or more days of work due to significant sudden injury in the past 3 months or refused to say or don't know how many days they missed due to injury (INJSIGMISWRK), INJSIGCHGWRK reports whether they made a major change in their work activities, such as taking on fewer hours or lighter duties, due to significant injury.
INJSIGCHGWRK is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGSCH
var.labl: Significant injury occurred at school/daycare, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample children who had two or more significant injuries in the past 3 months or don't know or refused to say how many significant injuries they had (INJSIGNUM), INJSIGSCH reports whether a significant injury happened at school or daycare. If necessary, interviewers elaborated by asking whether the injury happened at school or daycare, including classrooms, playgrounds, sports fields, swimming pools, parking lots, and other places on school or daycare property.
INJSIGSCH is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGFALSCH
var.labl: Significant fall occurred at school/daycare, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample children who had two or more significant injuries or don't know or refused to report how many injuries they had in the past 3 months (INJSIGNUM) and had a significant injury due to a fall (INJSIGFALL) and were also injured at school or daycare (INJSIGSCH), INJSIGFALSCH reports whether they fell at school or daycare.
INJSIGFALSCH is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJSIGMISSCH
var.labl: Number of school days missed due to significant injury, past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample children who had a significant injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGNFCNT), INJSIGMISSCH reports the number of school days they missed due to the injury.
INJSIGMISSCH is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.
var.codInstr: This is a 2-digit numeric variable with 0 implied decimal places

var.name: INJSIGFUTSCH
var.labl: Will miss more school days due to significant injury in past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample children who have missed at least one day of school or daycare due to significant injury in the past 3 months (INJSIGMISWRK), INJSIGFUTSCH reports whether they expect to miss any more days of school or daycare due to the injury.
INJSIGFUTSCH is part of the rotating core NHIS questions on sudden injury. For other core sudden injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJREPANY
var.labl: Any injury due to repetitive strain, past 3 months
var.txt: For sample adults, INJREPANY reports whether, in the past 3 months, they had any injuries due to repetitive strain. Before the first question in the repetitive strain injury section, respondents were told: [This] question is about repetitive strain injuries. By this, we mean injuries caused by repeating the same movement over an extended period. Examples include carpal tunnel syndrome, tennis elbow, or tendonitis.INJREPANY is collected as part of the rotating core NHIS questions on repetitive strain injuries, fielded for two consecutive years every three years. For other core repetitive strain injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.name: INJREPSIG
var.labl: Limited by repetitive strain injury for at least 24 hours (significant injury), past 3 months
var.txt:
For sample adults with a repetitive strain injury (INJREPANY), INJREPSIG reports whether, in the past 3 months, they had any repetitive strain injuries serious enough to limit their usual activities for at least 24 hours.
Before the first question in the repetitive strain injury section, respondents were told: [This] question is about repetitive strain injuries. By this, we mean injuries caused by repeating the same movement over an extended period. Examples include carpal tunnel syndrome, tennis elbow, or tendonitis.INJREPSIG is collected as part of the rotating core NHIS questions on repetitive strain injuries, fielded for two consecutive years every three years. For other core repetitive strain injury and injury-related variables, please see INJANY.

var.txt:
For sample adults with a significant repetitive strain injury in the past 3 months (INJREPSIG), INJREPSGDR reports whether, in the past 3 months, they talked to or saw a doctor or other health professional about their repetitive strain injuries.
